A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the spectra of the anhydrous acids are not consistent with the presence of the hydrogen atom in the acid, and are consistent with a structure in which the hydrogen is attached to the cyanide nitrogen atom, and in which the metal is coordinated with the nitrogen and two carbon atoms of the cyanide group.
the cyanide group in the complex acid has a higher frequency and a lower force constant than the free cyanide ion, while the metal-carbon stretch is lowered in frequency and the bond weakened.

the spectra of the anhydrous complex cyanide acids are similar to that of Hg2(CN)2 and Hg2Cl2, and the spectra of the hydrated complex cyanide acids, which contain water of hydration, are very similar to those of the complex cyanide acids which are anhydrous, except that the water of hydration has its own characteristic bands.

the structure of the complex is very important.
